cycle_scope_decision.claim_boundary: No current state field, mechanism proposal, compiled elementary step, evidence tier, registry, performance claim or design result is added or promoted.

contract_check.method: In-memory copies only; no scientific state or permission input was changed. Event-vocabulary probes use synthetic diagnostic before/after labels solely to isolate validation of transition_kind.

qualitative_relation_trial.interpretation: A bounded qualitative relation is representable without numeric n; explicit event-kind support and permission adjudication are separate. A source-proposal product handle must remain distinct from exact chemical identity before any future exact-instance promotion.
qualitative_relation_trial.method: In-memory structural/conditional probe only. Adds a separate paper-source diagnostic evidence ID and source_proposal_label; assumes only the three missing draft clauses are adjudicated. This is not a complete reviewed probe generation or live permission change.

cycle_scope_decision.draft_boundary: The live M0970 gate still lacks adjudicated product identity and before/after topology for its selected source reaction. A separately evidence-bound paper-source relation can use a source_proposal_label without resolving X00676. A source-scoped draft does not require executable cycle semantics, but does require an explicit source challenge, adjudication and review bindings for the changed scope.
cycle_scope_decision.exact_instance_boundary: Numeric chain lengths, initiation/elongation assignment and processivity are additional exact-instance requirements, not prerequisites in the source-scoped draft clause list. Unknown numeric n alone is not the reason drafting remains blocked.
cycle_scope_decision.existing_storage: The existing source_proposal_label and polymer_topology fields can represent a paper-scoped qualitative before/product relation with unknown numeric chain lengths. The current annotation view carries source-model statements and role referents without changing the reviewed M0970 state.
cycle_scope_decision.representation_boundary: The current probe rejects glycosyl_transfer, site_relocation and substrate_binding as typed state_transitions. This limits an explicit typed event sequence, not representation of a qualitative polymer relation. The v4 schema stores free-text kinds and chain fields; it does not interpret symbolic recurrence.
cycle_scope_decision.what_would_change_the_decision: Explicit paper-scoped source challenge and adjudication of the product/topology relation could authorize a bounded source draft. Shared event semantics and a concrete consumer are reasons to invest in richer typing, not formal draft requirements. Before any future exact-instance promotion, distinguish a source-proposal product handle from resolved exact chemical identity; never silently equate it with X00676. The current exact gate is unchanged.

reconsideration.curation: Existing source captures, source bindings and current-view projection are reused with zero additional requests. One annotation appears in three pinned report views. No curation-time reduction is measured.
reconsideration.representation: Chemical role and source-product referents stay in data. No enzyme-specific runtime branch or event-enum workaround is introduced; unresolved chemical states remain unresolved.
reconsideration.value: The scope check shows unknown numeric n is not itself a barrier to a source-proposal relation. It separates representability, reviewed permission and executable event semantics, preventing both unjustified rejection and exact-instance promotion. More same-paper role re-encoding offers limited incremental value, so the next evidence question should change.

source_findings.evidence_kind: source-proposed model supported by structure and mutagenesis, not an observed reaction trajectory
source_findings.finding: The SaMGT paper places the growing glycan at donor site S2 and incoming lipid II at acceptor site S1. Its model has the incoming GlcNAc 4-OH react with the donor C1; the new glycan is then proposed to move from S1 to S2. This is a source-model relation, not an atom map or observed reacting state. Lipid II can occupy both sites during initiation, so donor/acceptor is a reaction role rather than an invariant property of a compound identifier.
source_locators: Introduction, paragraph beginning In the synthesis of bacterial cell wall
Discussion, Mechanism of Lipid II Polymerization; Fig. 4A-E

source_findings.finding: The authors describe analogue 3 as containing GalNAc in place of the lipid II GlcNAc group, with the position-4 hydroxyl inverted. They state it binds in the lipid II pocket but cannot serve as a substrate catalyzed by E100. The deposited analogue pose must not be presented as an observed productive lipid II arrangement. This run inspected the paper and entry metadata, not current atom coordinates. The paper describes a stabilized Mu50 Q28-R269 construct with transmembrane and TG regions and a cleaved His6 tag; this is not a full-length-protein identity claim.
source_locators: Results, Overall Structure of SaMGT in Complex with Lipid II Analog
Discussion, paragraph beginning From the crystal structure of SaMGT
Materials and Methods, Cloning, Expression, and Purification

controls_and_limits: Capped Lipid II/Lipid IV can react at their reducing end, but that alone does not establish polymer-growth direction because the uncapped short substrates can self-condense.
The longer-oligomer test uses substrates described as unable to self-condense; no-lipid-II controls and lipid-II-supplemented reactions distinguish extension.
The four tested PGT domains are not the Q99T05/SaMGT preparation. Extension of the conclusion to the full family is an author proposal, not a direct test of every family member.
This direction assay does not identify M0970 product placeholder X00676, the exact M0970 chain length, or processivity.
source_findings.evidence_kind: published biochemical direction test; not a project-run experiment
source_findings.finding: Non-reducing-end Gal-capped longer glycan oligomers were extended only when lipid II was supplied. The authors interpret this as extension at the anomeric diphospholipid end, called the reducing end by convention although it is not a free lactol. The tested PGT domains were E. coli PBP1A, E. coli PBP1B, A. aeolicus PBP1A and S. aureus PBP2.
source_locators: Fig. 2B and Fig. 3B captions; concluding paragraph

source_findings.finding: The current M-CSA Step 1 prose describes nucleophilic attack by the strand at the donor site toward the acceptor strand. The SaMGT primary model instead places the attacking GlcNAc 4-OH on acceptor lipid II. Do not resolve this by trusting participant order or silently reversing the imported M-CSA text. The annotation corrects the project polymer-role label at the primary-model scope only. Mechanism 2 Step 2 instead describes attack by the acceptor on the donor; that does not resolve all of the local alternatives.
source_locators: Huang et al. Fig. 4B-C and corresponding Discussion paragraph

source_findings.finding: The M0970-linked 2020 paper describes MD and QM/MM modeling and a proposed metal-bound-hydroxide pathway. Its abstract is not an independent experimental observation of polymer direction or evidence resolving the competing local mechanisms.

source_findings.finding: The paper orders glycosyl transfer, movement of the resulting product to the donor site, and binding of another lipid II at the acceptor site. This supports a source-proposed role sequence while the exact M0970 polymer product remains unresolved.
